questions.title: Origins
questions.prompt: Name the place first. Not the family. Families lie. I can check places.

answers.title: A ward inside the city walls
answers.description: You grew up where neighbors knew one another's households and histories.
answers.biography: Born within the walls, where every neighbor knew whose child you were and what the family had done last winter.

answers.title: The southern marsh-fringe
answers.description: The city was something you visited, not the center of your world.
answers.biography: From the marsh-fringe, where tithes were paid in reed-bundles and the city happened at a distance.

answers.title: A barley village on the canals
answers.description: You knew the irrigated plain and the storehouse's claim on each harvest.
answers.biography: Raised on the irrigated plain, in a house that measured its year by what the storehouse took.

answers.title: A herding camp on the desert edge
answers.description: Your people moved with flocks and were rarely entered in city records.
answers.biography: Of the herding camps, known to the city as wool and mutton, and entered in no record before this one.

answers.title: A trading town far from the plain
answers.description: You came from beyond the local network, with a name the clerk may not know how to write.
answers.biography: A stranger to the plain, recorded as the clerk heard your name, not quite as it was said.

questions.title: Responsibilities
questions.prompt: Everyone drags something through that gate. Tell me what was tied to your ankle.

answers.title: A grain debt
answers.description: The storehouse already has a claim on your household.
answers.biography: Arrived owing a seed-loan unpaid across two sowings, a debt the storehouse knew before a word was spoken.

answers.title: Mouths that depended on you
answers.description: Other people depended on your work and its ration.
answers.biography: Carried an aging parent and younger siblings, whose rations depended on your place.

answers.title: A household you owed
answers.description: A household expects repayment in favors as well as goods.
answers.biography: Indebted to a household that expected repayment in favors as well as grain.

answers.title: A kinsman's missing obligation
answers.description: Someone in your family left an obligation behind—and vanished.
answers.biography: Answered for a kinsman's shortfall, and for the kinsman who vanished with it.

answers.title: Nothing
answers.description: No debt, dependents, or quarrel. The clerk finds this suspicious.
answers.biography: Owed nothing and owing nothing, recorded as a puzzle rather than a virtue.

questions.title: Formative / The day that stayed
questions.prompt: Every scribe points at one day. The day a mark on clay did what a hand couldn't. Give me yours.

answers.title: The day a count was wrong
answers.description: A quay tally cost someone their place; you had counted the baskets.
answers.biography: Learned early that a number can ruin a person, having counted the baskets yourself on the day one did.

parameters.text: A quantity everyone relied on did not match what had actually been received or used.

answers.title: The day you read what you shouldn't have
answers.description: A visiting official left a tablet unattended. You puzzled out marks not meant for you.
answers.biography: Learned marks from a tablet left unguarded, and kept what it said ever since.

parameters.text: I puzzled out marks on a tablet that had been left unattended.

answers.title: The day a boundary dispute was settled
answers.description: A household lost land it rightly held because the other side had a tablet.
answers.biography: Watched a household lose land it rightly held because the other side had a tablet and theirs did not.

parameters.text: I saw a household lose land it rightly held because the other side had a tablet.

answers.title: The day the storehouse nearly ran out
answers.description: You watched ration priority in a bad season.
answers.biography: Saw what a short season did to a storehouse, and which names were last on the ration.

parameters.text: I saw scarcity decide whose name came last on the ration.

answers.title: The day you saw what a seal could do
answers.description: A pressed mark changed whose grain was whose.
answers.biography: Understood in one afternoon that the mark pressed in clay mattered more than whoever pressed it.

parameters.text: I saw a seal mark change whose grain was whose.

questions.title: Formative / The one you would rather not tell
questions.prompt: Now the one you'd rather not tell me. I'll write it down either way.

answers.title: You took something that wasn't yours
answers.description: Grain, a seal-blank, or a token; someone else took blame.
answers.biography: Took what was not to be taken, and let another bear the blame.

parameters.text: I took something that was not mine and let another bear the blame.

answers.title: You saw a wrong and said nothing
answers.description: A short count, a pressed seal, or a beating. You stayed silent.
answers.biography: Witnessed a wrong and kept quiet, and remembers who saw the silence.

parameters.text: I witnessed a wrong and kept quiet.

answers.title: You gave a name
answers.description: An official asked about a neighbor. You never learned what happened.
answers.biography: Gave a neighbor's name to an official, and never learned what became of the neighbor.

parameters.text: I gave a neighbor's name to an official and never learned what followed.

answers.title: You left someone behind
answers.description: A sibling or friend wanted the place you took.
answers.biography: Took the place that was offered and left behind the one who had hoped for it.

parameters.text: I took a place someone close to me had hoped to receive.

answers.title: Nothing
answers.description: The clerk writes 'nothing' and remembers that you said it.
answers.biography: Declined a second account, which the clerk recorded as one.

parameters.text: I declined to give a second account of my past.

questions.title: Entry
questions.prompt: How did you come through that gate? Not why. How. The how decides who owns the first season.

answers.title: Debt pledge
answers.description: You entered as collateral against an obligation.
answers.biography: Entered as collateral against a debt, and worth more to the compound while the debt stayed unpaid.

answers.title: Temple draft
answers.description: The temple claimed first call on your service.
answers.biography: Drawn into the compound by temple levy, and answerable to the temple before anyone else.

answers.title: Family placement
answers.description: Your family placed you and expects a return.
answers.biography: Placed by family, who counted what they spent.

answers.title: Walked in
answers.description: No pledge, levy, or sponsor. The clerk let you stay.
answers.biography: Entered unsummoned and tolerated, which was not the same as belonging.

questions.title: Instruction
questions.prompt: Three names are open. Who will you lodge under? A blank tablet waits. “Make your mark.”

answers.title: Shuruppak-ilu · West wing archives
answers.description: A senior scribe who points at a mistake and waits for you to hear it.
answers.biography: Instructed under Shuruppak-ilu, who valued an honest gap in the record above a tidy lie.

answers.title: Utu-mansum · The gate
answers.description: A tax scribe who has never once been rushed.
answers.biography: Lodged under Utu-mansum at the gate, where every mark had to be defended to an angry boatman.

answers.title: Ur-Nanna · Storehouse Bay Four
answers.description: A temple steward who listens to weather like other men listen to creditors.
answers.biography: Taken in by Ur-Nanna, who taught how to keep a storehouse from rotting from the inside, and to share the blame when it did.

questions.title: Path
questions.prompt: Scribes serve many people and institutions. What responsibility do you hope to make your own?

answers.title: Commercial
answers.description: Exchange, delivery, and the people waiting at the other end.
answers.biography: Drawn toward commercial work: exchange, delivery, and the relationships between people moving and receiving goods.

answers.title: Martial
answers.description: Security, custody, and safe movement—not a military command.
answers.biography: Drawn toward work involving security, custody, and the safe movement of people and resources.

answers.title: Civic
answers.description: Organizing resources and keeping institutional responsibilities clear.
answers.biography: Drawn toward civic administration: organizing resources, keeping responsibilities clear, and helping collective work function.

answers.title: Religious
answers.description: Sacred practice and the institutions that support it; no priestly title is granted.
answers.biography: Drawn toward responsibilities connected with sacred practice and the institutions that support them.

questions.title: Identity
questions.prompt: The clerk places a disputed tally before you. Which mark do you make? He records the answer, then names what it has shown.

answers.title: You ask for the count to be checked again
answers.description: You refuse to close the tablet until every measure agrees.
answers.biography: The clerk called the habit exacting.

answers.title: You accept the correction that keeps the queue moving
answers.description: You make room for the person waiting behind the record.
answers.biography: The clerk called the habit pliable.

answers.title: You reject the entry and require the responsible mark
answers.description: You make the record answer to the rule, even when the answer is hard.
answers.biography: The clerk called the habit severe.

answers.title: You set the tablet aside until the witness is present
answers.description: You will not make a mark whose consequences you cannot yet see.
answers.biography: The clerk called the habit cautious.

creation_narration: This biography is game narration, not an in-world tablet. The clerk records only answers and marks that actually exist.

first_workday_mentor_lines.mentor_shuruppak_ilu: Sit. The reed is crooked in your hand, and your sums are soft at the edges. Fix the arithmetic on the third column, and don’t invent numbers to make the clay look happy.
first_workday_mentor_lines.mentor_utu_mansum: Stand by the scale. Don’t look at the sky, don’t talk to the boatmen, and don’t let anyone rush your tally. What crosses that sill belongs to the temple until I say otherwise.
first_workday_mentor_lines.mentor_ur_nanna: Check the thatch over Bay Four. If the rain gets into the seed-corn again, Shuruppak-ilu will have both our skins on the drying rack. Go look at the jars.
